rci1_using_msad.detail: Two cohorts (Utrecht Schizophrenia project and GROUP consortium); participants recruited in various inpatient and outpatient facilities.
rci1_using_msad.supporting_text: "Participants for the current study were selected from a large longitudinal sample based on two cohorts including patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls, the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, in Utrecht, the Netherlands. In both cohorts, patients with schizophrenia recruited in various inpatient and outpatient facilities"

rci2_using_epd.detail: Reference cohort drawn from Utrecht Schizophrenia project and GROUP consortium; no established public datasets reported.
rci2_using_epd.supporting_text: "Participants for the current study were selected from a large longitudinal sample based on two cohorts including patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls, the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, in Utrecht, the Netherlands."

rci3_epd_name.supporting_text: "Participants for the current study were selected from a large longitudinal sample based on two cohorts including patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls, the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, in Utrecht, the Netherlands."

rci5_n.detail: All 164 healthy controls used as the normative reference; no explicit train/test split; normative reference calculated at each time point (baseline and follow-up) from the same HC sample
rci5_n.supporting_text: "The final data set consisted of 656 scans from 164 healthy participants and 164 patients."
rci5_n.location: Janssen2021.pdf.md: Methods / Sample and Neuroimaging; Table 1

rci6_sex.detail: Male n (126) and percentage (77%) reported directly in Table 1 for healthy controls; female_n estimated from total N (164) minus male_n (126) = 38; female_pct calculated as 38/164 = 23.2%

rci7_age.detail: Baseline age statistics for healthy controls from Table 1 (mean 31.04, SD 11.65); age range (16-70 years at baseline) from Methods section; age in years
